idiom_name: lapin Consumer: Stream of deliveries or set_delegate(ConsumerDelegate) spawned by the executor
implementation_notes: std has no runtime, so the consumer is realized through an async client: lapin's basic_consume returns a Consumer that either yields DeliveryResults as a Stream (consumer.next().await) or spawns a ConsumerDelegate on the executor, whose handle_delivery is the callback the library invokes - in both shapes the application never drives a receive loop of its own, and basic_qos prefetch bounds in-flight work. For in-process delivery the same inversion is tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver::recv().await, where the sender pushes and the consumer task resumes. The hand-written form is justified only for protocols no client crate covers.
pitfalls: Acking after the connection or channel has dropped returns an error and the message is redelivered - ack within the delivery's lifetime and make handlers idempotent.
Blocking inside an async task starves the executor because tasks are cooperative; move synchronous work to spawn_blocking.
basic_qos prefetch is the only back-pressure: without it the client buffers unbounded deliveries and can exhaust memory.
